problem: Prior LLM/VLM closed-loop replanning systems (e.g., Code as Policies, REFLECT, ReplanVLM) mostly assume fully observable tabletop scenes. They handle execution failures by simply re-attempting, and they ignore how modules depend on each other (e.g., navigating to a poor base pose makes a later grasp fail). As a result they break down on long-horizon open-vocabulary mobile manipulation (OVMM) under partial observability.
motivation: OVMM requires grounding free-form instructions in unstructured, partially observed 3D scenes and recovering from errors that compound over long navigate-grasp-place sequences. OK-Robot on HomeRobot OVMM showed that naively chaining a VLM planner with low-level skills produces cascading errors across modules. This motivates tracing failures back across the perception, navigation and manipulation levels rather than retrying locally.
key_idea: Use GPT-4V as a code-generating closed-loop planner over perception and execution APIs, organized in a three-level hierarchy (global, local, object). A matching three-level status-verification and recovery scheme backtracks to the right level when a failure or infeasibility is detected.
insight: The mobile setting gains more than tabletop (+35 vs +27.5 SR points over CaP*). The paper attributes this to closed-loop replanning mattering more on longer sequences, where failures are more likely. The failure table shows the recovery mechanism rescues 31 of 52 failure events (31/38 re-planning steps succeed). Grasp failures dominate (24 events, 17 recovered), and most are traced to a poor base pose chosen during navigation, which supports the cross-module (global-level) recovery idea. Perception false positives remain the main unrecovered source (3 direct task failures). Caveat: there is no module-wise ablation, and the only baseline is a CaP variant, so individual component contributions are not isolated.
method: Global-level perception (explore_global): frontier-based exploration with the mobile base builds a global object map of large furniture (category, location, merged point cloud, visual features, language description).

Local-level perception (explore_local): GPT-4V uses commonsense to pick a likely receptacle region (e.g., cup→table); the robot navigates there and builds a local object-placement map of small objects. SAM-2 tracks object status, and local perception is re-run if objects move.

Object-level perception (report_observation): wrist-camera close-up images are sent to GPT-4V to extract fine-grained attributes (e.g., empty vs used cup) for the Goal Reasoner, which selects the target object by functional and commonsense reasoning.

Status Verifier: feasibility verification (can the task proceed, or roll back, e.g., no empty cup on this table → search another table) and success verification. Success verification uses before/after wrist images plus API return values, and diagnoses the failure cause to choose the recovery level.

Hierarchical Plan Restorer: object-level (retry with a different grasp pose), local-level (re-detect/relocate a moved object by updating the local map), and global-level (navigate to alternative furniture or a better base pose when infeasible or unreachable).

Code-generation planner: a system prompt (task description, feedback handling, robot setup, skill library, response guidelines, tips) makes GPT-4V emit Python calling APIs navigate / grasp (point-cloud based) / place. Code and plan are checked, and exceptions feed explicit error messages back for plan correction.

setting.backbone: GPT-4V (frozen, prompted) + SAM-2 and perception modules + classical primitives (frontier exploration, point-cloud grasping)
setting.observation: base RGB-D camera + Lidar + IMU; wrist RGB-D camera (close-up images fed to GPT-4V); API return values as text feedback
setting.action_space: LLM-generated Python code calling high-level APIs: explore_global, explore_local, report_observation, navigate(object), grasp(object), place(object/location)
setting.privileged: none (builds its own global object map via frontier-based exploration at the start of each task)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is used; all results come from self-designed real-world tasks, reported as fractions in the tables. Only the totals are listed here; per-task fractions are in Tables 1–2. Failure statistics (14 direct failures; recovery 31/38 re-planning steps, 31/52 total) are in Table 3. Hardware inconsistency: the setup describes a wheeled base with a Kinova Gen3 arm, but the acknowledgments thank Unitree for B2/Z1 robots.
results: COME reaches 65% SR (13/20) on 4 real-world mobile manipulation tasks versus 30% (6/20) for CaP* (Code as Policies augmented with the same exploration and navigation APIs). On 4 tabletop tasks it reaches 75% (30/40) versus 47.5% (19/40). Step-wise success also improves (101/122 vs 76/125 mobile; 123/140 vs 98/138 tabletop), and the recovery mechanism resolves 31 of 52 observed failure events.
limitations: Very small-scale evaluation: a single real room, 5 trials per mobile task, one baseline (CaP*), and no ablation isolating the perception-hierarchy or recovery modules.
Relies on proprietary GPT-4V: latency and cost are not reported, and residual perception false positives remain (3 of 14 direct task failures) even after VLM verification.
Task-specific API and prompt engineering; no evaluation on standard OVMM benchmarks (e.g., HomeRobot OVMM), so results are hard to compare with other work.
compares_to: CaP* (Code as Policies augmented with exploration and navigation APIs)
